The petitioner filed this petition under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 for claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is that, on 29-03-2023 at about 10.10 p.m., he was travelling as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03/HQ- 0927 and proceeding on Hoodi Main Road, Near Bhagini Restaurant, Bangalore City, at that time, the rider of the another motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-96/D-2291 drove the same, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life, came at high speed and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident, as a result of forced impact, petitioner was fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Aaxis Hospital for first aid, further shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient, the duty doctors examined him clinically and radiologically, which revealed that he sustained fracture of right femur, he underwent surgery for the said fractures and internal fixation was done.
Other injuries treated with conservatively, for which he will require the funds for treatment, medicines etc.,

Accordingly, the petitioner is still under treatment and he was forced to spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses, he require one more surgery for removal of implants, he was also taken treatment at Miracle Hospital.

Due to the above said injuries, the petitioner is completely bed ridden and cannot do his activities as earlier to the accident and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering and the said injuries are permanent in nature and he is unable to do his job till the end of his life.
4. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 23 years and he was working at Private Company and earning Rs.30,000/-per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his job and lost the earnings.

It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-96/D-2291 against whom the Mahadevapura Traffic Police have registered a case in Crime No.042/2023 punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Hence, respondent No.1 being the Insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.

On service of notice, Respondent No.1 entered its appearance through its learned counsel and it has filed its objection to the main petition.

Respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Tribunal,
hence he has placed as exparte.
6. Respondent No.1 in its objection has denied all the petition averments.
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle.

Further it is contended that the rider of the petitioner's vehicle and the rider of the offending motorcycle are not having valid D.L. at the time of accident, the offending vehicle did not have valid permit and fitness certificate.
It is further contended that, neither the insurer nor the owner of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-03/HQ-0927 has been made as a party which amounts to non-joinder of necessary parties.
The medical bills are all created and concocted one just for the purpose of filing of this false and frivolous petition.
Respondent No.1 has denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner and also the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.
It has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.
7. Based on the pleadings, following issues are framed:-

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 29-03-2023 at about 10.10PM, he was travelling as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03/HQ- 0927 the rider was riding the same on Hoodi Main Road, Near Bhagini Restaurant, Bangalore City,

wherein, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-96/D-2291 drove it, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangerous to human life, came at high speed, dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident, due to forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3) What order or award?
8.

12. In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and filed his affidavit in lieu of chief examination.
In his chief examination affidavit, he has reiterated the entire averments of the petition and got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of F.I.R.

Ex.P.2 is the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 and 4 are the copies of hospital intimations, Ex.P.5 is the copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.6 is the copy of Sketch, Ex.P.7 and 8 are the copy of IMV reports,
Ex.P.9 is the copy of Wound Certificate,

Ex.P.10 is the copy of Charge Sheet, Ex.P.11 and 12 are the copies of Wound Certificates, Ex.P.13 and 14 are the copies of Hospital Intimations, Ex.P.15 and 16 are the Discharge Summaries, Ex.P.17 is the Medical Bills, Ex.P.18 is the copy of Aadhar Card of the petitioner, Ex.P.19 is the Copy of D.L. and Ex.P.20 is the copy of Company ID Card.
In the cross-examination, he has stated that, he was a pillion rider of Rapido Motor Bike, he don't know who is the owner.
He denied that, the rider was not injured.
He admitted the suggestion of the counsel for respondent No.1 that, motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-96/D-2291 hit to him from back side.
He has given the complaint, the offending bike was at the spot and his friends took the photo of it, therefore, he has mentioned the said vehicle in the complaint.
After the accident the police came to the hospital, but, he has not filed the complaint, but later after discussion with his family and surgery, he has given the complaint.

13. The petitioner got examined the Dr. Nagaraj B.N. who is an Orthopaedic Surgeon, SOADS at Bangalore as PW.2 and he got marked 02 documents at Ex.P.21 and P.22, which are the Medical Examination Report and X-ray.
14. Per contra, the respondents have not adduced any evidence and got marked no documents on their side.
15 Learned counsel for petitioner submitted his arguments by contending that, the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle.
Hence, prayed to award the compensation.
Counsel for respondent No.1 has submitted the written arguments contending that, there is 12 days delay in lodging the First information and insured vehicle has been falsely implicated.
Therefore, prays to dismiss the petition.
17. Respondent No.1 has contained that, there is delay of 12 days in filing the complainant.
On perusal of Ex.P.2 the complaint it appears that, the accident took place on 29- 03-2023 at about 10.20 pm.

On perusal of Ex.P.3, the police intimation, it appears that, the petitioner has been admitted in the Aaxis Hospital, Bengaluru on the same day i.e., 29-03-2023 at about 11.20pm and history is road traffic accident.
On perusal of Ex.P.4, it appears that, the patient was shifted to Manipal Hospital at the mid night of 30-03-2023 at about 12.50am and the history is road traffic accident.

On perusal of Ex.P.13 the hospital intimation, it appears that, it is the MLC intimation of Mohan Das.T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77189193/

sentences.text: On perusal of Ex.P.15 and P.16 the discharge summaries, it appears that, the petitioner has been admitted in the Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru on 30-03-2023 and discharged on 05/04/2023 and further admitted in Miracle Hospital on 06-04-2023 and discharged on 12-04- 2023.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.9 the would certificate issued by the Manipal Hospital, it appears that, the history is road traffic accident.

On perusal of these documents, it appears that, the petitioner was admitted in the Aaxis Hospital and later shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru and Miracle Hospital from 29-03-2022 to 12-04-2023 for the injuries sustained in R.T.A and the medical records are entered on same day of the accident.
Further, the counsel for the respondent No.1 himself has suggested to PW.1 that, the offending vehicle No.TN-96/D-2291 hit from back side.
The petitioner was admitted in the hospital for the treatment and himself has filed the complaint.
PW.1 has stated that, after discussion with his family he has given the complaint.

On perusal of Ex.P.2, the first information, it appears that, filing of the information was delayed as injured was admitted in the hospital and it has been filed after discussion with the parents of the petitioner.
Therefore, it appears that, the delay in filing FIR is properly explained.
18. On perusal of Ex.P.2 complaint, Ex.P.5 the spot mahazar, Ex.
P.6 the Spot Sketch, Ex

.P.7 and 8 the IMV Reports, Ex.P.10 charge sheet, it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the rider of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-06/D-2291, so it clearly indicates that the offending vehicle involved in the accident.

Further on perusal of charge sheet it discloses that,
the Mahadevapura Traffic Police have filed the case against the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-06/D- 2291 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
But, there is no any material to hold that, there is a contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
19. The respondent No.1 has contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner himself and rider of the offending vehicle has no valid D.L.
To prove this contention, Respondent No.1 had not adduced any oral or documentary evidence on its behalf.
Nothing is on record to show that the rider of the motorcycle ride the motorcycle without D.L.
On perusal of charge sheet at Ex.P.10 there is nothing on record or accusation against the rider of the motorcycle for not having valid D.L.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that respondent No.1 has failed to prove that the rider of the said motorcycle was not having valid D.L.
20.

In the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the claimant has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble APEX Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others.

21. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1-F.I.R. Ex.P.2- Complaint, Ex.P.5-Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.6-Sketch,
Ex.P.7 and 8-IMV Report, Ex.P.9, 11 & 12-Wound Certificate, Ex.P.10-Charge Sheet, it appears that,
as on the date of alleged accident, the driver of offending vehicle drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed and dashed to the petitioner and caused the accident.

Therefore, considering all these aspects, this Tribunal came to conclusion that, the said accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-96/D-2291.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-
The Petitioner is claiming the compensation amount of Rs.20,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner produced wound certificates and discharge summaries issued by Manipal Hospital, Bangalore and Vydehi Hospital, Bangalore and prayed to award compensation amount.
The Respondents not disputed the said documents.
On perusal of the Ex.P.9-Wound Certificate it is discloses that, the petitioner has sustained the fracture of the right femur (Thighbone).
The doctor opined that the injury is grievous in nature.

Therefore,
taking all these facts and nature of injuries, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
23. The petitioner had produced medical bills, which are marked as Ex.P.17.
On perusal of the bill at Sl.No.4 of Ex.P.17, it appears that, it is belonging to the Cot and Folding Walker.
Therefore, the said bill has not been considered.
The respondents not denied the other medical bills.

On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospitals, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.1,07,549/- under the head of medical expenditure.

24. As per Ex.P.15 and P.16 discharge summaries the petitioner took treatment at Manipal Hospitals, Bengaluru from 30-03-2023 to 05-04-2023 for 07 days and also at Miracle Women and Children's Hospital from 06-04-2023 to 12-04-2023 for 07 days i.e., for total 14 days.

Therefore, by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.14,000/- under the head Transportation, food, Nourishment and conveyance charges.
25. The Petitioner contended that, due to injuries he was suffering from pain and mental agony and he is unable to carry on his day to day activities which he used to do prior to the accident.
To prove the assessment of disability, the petitioner got examined one Doctor Sri. Nagaraj B.N. as PW-2.

In the chief examination affidavit PW.2 deposed that, on 01-10-2024 the Petitioner came to him for assessment of disability purpose and on examination he found that, the Petitioner has wasting of the right thigh muscles, restricted right hip and knee and the recent X- ray shows united fracture with implaint-in-situ.

In the cross-examination admitted that, personally he had not treated the Petitioner, he examined him after one and half year after the accident and further admitted that, the right femur fracture is united.
PW.1 in his cross-examination has deposed that, he is working.
Hence the petitioner is not entitled to claim any compensation amount under the head loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

26. The Petitioner stated that, prior to the accident he was working at Private Company and earning Rs.30,000/-p.m. and due to injuries sustained in the accident, he is unable to attend the work and facing financial difficulties.
The Petitioner had not produced any documents to prove his income and avocation.
This accident occurred in the year 2023.

However by considering the age and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded reasonable compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of income during laid up period.

sentences.text: The petitioner also sought for expenses towards future medicine for further treatment.
In the chief- examination affidavit the petitioner deposed that, he is forced to spent huge amount for future medication.
The PW.2 doctor deposed in the chief affidavit that, the petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of implant and the estimate of said surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
In the Cross examination the PW.2 admitted that he had not treated the petitioner and fractures are united.
However, by considering the age and nature of injuries and evidence of the doctor, this Tribunal has award reasonable compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of future medical expenses.
(Which does not carry any interest).
28. The Petitioner sustained grievous injury as shown in the wound certificate.
The petitioner working at Private Company and earning Rs.30,000/-p.m. and due to accidental injuries his routine work was hampered for some days.

Therefore, by considering this aspect and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

 period.

Total Rs
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,51,549/-.
30. Interest:

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Mohan Das.T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77189193/
7 Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a. (Excluding the future medical expenses) and not more than that.

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
31. Liability:-
As already observed above, Respondent No.1 is the Insurer and Respondent No.2 is the Owner of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TN-96/D-2291.

As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle, hence Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further the Respondent No.1 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder:
The petitioner is entitled for total  compensation amount of Rs.2,51,549/- with  interest @6% p.a., (Excluding the future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 & 2 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.1 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.

After deposit, entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner with proper identification (As the petitioner has incurred huge amount towards medical expenses and also he has to incur some expenses towards future medication).
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Mohan Das.T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77189193/
7 Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a. (Excluding the future medical expenses) and not more than that.
Hence, this Tribunal hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle, hence Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
